title: Robust analysis of differential Faraday rotation based on interferometric closure observables
question: Can newly-introduced complex interferometric closure observables (closure traces) be used to extract robust, calibration-independent information on source polarization structure and differential Faraday Rotation across frequency?

what.value: Polarization structure image of M87 AGN and jet and Rotation Measure (~1.5 x 10^5 rad/m^2) from ALMA EHT observations

evidence.quote: Figure 1 shows the polarization structure of the AGN and the jet of M87, obtained from the ALMA data (cite: Goddi2021complete).
compared to the value of $\sim 1.5 \times 10^5$ rad/m$^{2}$ for M87*, obtained from the ALMA EHT data (cite: Goddi2021complete; TFM).
In Fig. 2, we show the RM map of M87, obtained from the results presented in (cite: TFG).

recipe.goal: Simulate full-polarization visibilities for an M87-like three-component model
recipe.method: Discrete Fourier transform of Stokes parameters (I, Q, U, V) for three point-source (delta) components (core, knot A, knot B) on the exact ALMA baseline coordinates across 4 spectral windows, adding 0.5 mJy uncorrelated Gaussian noise per integration time
key_parameters: Core position (l, m) = (0, 0), I = 1.2 Jy; Knot A position (l, m) = (-11.28, 4.35), I = 0.1 Jy; Knot B position (l, m) = (-13.92, 4.95), I = 0.05 Jy
Simulated core RM ~ 0.35 x 10^7 rad/m^2; Gaussian visibility noise std = 0.5 mJy
assumptions: Source polarization structure represented by three compact (delta) components with Stokes V = 0

recipe.goal: Compute complex closure traces on a 13-antenna subset
recipe.method: Select a subset of 13 ALMA antennas preserving Fourier space coverage and compute complex closure traces T_ABCD from visibility matrices on all 4-antenna quadrangles using a custom Python module
key_parameters: 13 antennas selected out of 33 ALMA antennas

recipe.goal: Fit core-only polarization per spectral window via 2D grid search and linear RM fit
recipe.method: Perform a 2D grid search minimizing the squared differences of closure traces for each spectral window independently (fixing RM parameter p_2 = 0 and jet knots A and B to image values), followed by a linear fit of core EVPA versus wavelength squared to recover RM
key_parameters: Free parameters per spw: core EVPA (p_0) and core polarized flux density (p_1 = m * I_core); fixed parameters: p_2 = 0, knot A and knot B Stokes parameters
assumptions: Equal weights for all visibilities; chi^2 temperature T estimated from the standard deviation of closure trace residuals at the minimum

recipe.goal: Simultaneously fit multi-component polarization and RM across all spectral windows using MCMC
recipe.method: Combine all 4 spectral windows and fit the polarization (EVPA, polarized flux, and RM) of the core and one jet knot simultaneously while fixing the remaining knot (with V = 0), using circular statistics reparameterization and affine-invariant MCMC sampling on both simulated and real ALMA data
key_parameters: Reference wavelength lambda_0 = 0; 6 free parameters (q_0, q_1, q_2, q_3, and two component RMs)
assumptions: One component is fixed with Stokes V = 0 to break the latitudinal degeneracy in the Poincare sphere and serve as differential polarization reference

score_reason: The mathematical formalism, simulated source table (Table 1/unnumbered table), and ALMA project code/date/time are clearly specified, allowing the simulated experiments to be closely approximated; however, the custom Python code is not released, the exact 13-antenna subset is only shown graphically, MCMC settings/priors are omitted, and there are minor text/equation inconsistencies in the two-component parameterization.
rediscovery_reason: The archival ALMA data (2016.1.01154.V) and synthetic model parameters are fully specified in the paper, the mathematical definition of closure traces and the chi^2 objective function are explicit, and the main results are quantitative (recovered EVPA, polarized flux, and RM values).
